messages:
elaine: FYI I bumped the continuous-batcher kernel to v3.2.1 on canary and we see a p99 uplift ~18% for 6k-8k token sequences. opening thread to track root cause and quick mitigation.

sanjay: ugh. noticed higher queueing too?

elaine: yes, queuing spikes during KV-cache warmups. avg batch size dropped 12% which hurt throughput and kernel selection falls back to slower matmul path.

perf-bot: profile summary: canary node pool 03 · samples=1200
- avg tokens/sec per-GPU: -9%
- p50 latency: +6%
- p95 latency: +12%
- p99 latency: +18%
- KV hit-rate during spike: 0.62 -> 0.38 (cold phase)

marco: kernel selector seems to pick the quantized FMA kernel only when batch_size >= 16 and seq_len < 1024. with smaller batches we hit the generic kernel which regresses.

elaine: we need to tune admission so that token-budget targets bias admission toward batching-friendly requests when KV-hit probability is low. idea: probabilistic admit that accounts for KV-hit weight and remaining token budget.

devex: can you sketch config? would like something we can flip per-pool.

elaine: initial sketch:
```
admit_policy: probabilistic_kv_weighted
params:
  token_budget_per_sec: 1200000
  kv_hit_bonus: 0.2    # extra budget credit for requests with KV hit
  batch_preference_bias: 0.6 # 0..1, higher -> favor batchable admits
  soft_429_threshold: 0.85 # probability of soft-429 when budget near cap
  min_batch_hold_ms: 6
```

sanjay: solid. how do we detect KV-hit probability pre-admit? we only know hit after kvcache lookup which is expensive to do inside admission.

elaine: two options: 1) fast approximate kvcache bloom check at admission (cheap) 2) maintain per-route hotness scores and use recent hit-rate as prior. prefer (2) for production.

marco: also saw a kernel mismatch signal in traces: when batch size=10 and seq=4096 we still took the slow kernel due to sequence classification bug. I pushed a small patch to selector heuristics — might reduce p99 by ~6%.

perf-bot: microtrace snippet (shortened):
```
batch_assemble: 3.4ms -> batch_size=9
kernel_choice: generic_matmul (expected fma_opt)
kv_lookup: 0.9ms
infer: 72ms (generic)
```

elaine: mitigation plan (short):
- 1) roll config with probabilistic_kv_weighted admit on canary pool (low risk)
- 2) patch kernel selector to prefer fma_opt when batch_size>8 and seq<6k (marco PR ready)
- 3) add per-route hit-rate prior to admission decisions
- 4) short-term: raise min_batch_hold_ms from 3 -> 6ms on canary to nudge batch sizes up

marco: PR: https://git.internal/r/eng/runtime/selector/merge/345 (contains unit tests).

ops-bot: deploy started: canary pool 'cb-v3' at commit 9f2c3a. please monitor p95/p99 and kv-hit rates.

devex: if this goes well can we expose the batch_preference_bias knob in Console for Dedicated tenants? helps customers tune cost vs latency.

elaine: yes — expose as "batching_bias" per-route. default 0.6, editable. we should warn in UI about possible p99 regressions if set too low.

sanjay: question on soft-429: do we do hard reject or send soft-429 body with Retry-After?

elaine: soft-429 semantics: return 429-like envelope but stream-friendly with small retry token and hint for fallback model. e.g. response contains: {"status":"soft_429","retry_ms":120,"fallback":"gpt-small"}. not a full HTTP 429 block.

marco: also add telemetry tag admit.reason = kv_prior|batch_bias|token_budget so we can slice postmortems.

perf-bot: scheduled: run A/B canary with new admit policy for 6 hours, sample size target 30k requests. will report delta at 2h/6h.

elaine: thanks all. i'll open a short runbook for rollback conditions (p99 > +10% OR kv-hit drop > 0.15). tagging @oncall for watches. :eyes: 

ops-bot: @oncall notified. :bell:

marco: quick note — if kv-hit bonus is too large we risk starving short interactive requests. keep kv_hit_bonus conservative.

elaine: agreed. we'll start with 0.2, observe, then tweak.

sanjay: great thread. if we need a quick revert we should be able to toggle admit_policy flag per-pool. good to go from my side. :+1:
